report_md:
# Sector dispersion — report

**Dev:** 23.23% CAGR / 67.86% DD / 0.73 Sharpe.  
**Full:** 16.76% CAGR / 67.86% DD / 0.61 Sharpe; 273 full fills.  
**2024-2026 holdout:** 2.09% CAGR / 34.18% DD / 0.22 Sharpe.

## Rules

When sector dispersion is low, the market is moving on broad macro factors; buy TQQQ. When dispersion is high, hold BIL.

## Why it is distinct

The primary object is cross-sectional dispersion, not relative sector leadership. It is not a sector-rotation gate. Maximum signal Jaccard against the nine existing winners is 0.55 and maximum raw correlation is 0.64.

## Caveats

- Full CAGR is below the TQQQ bar; this is an active research family, not a winner.
- The 2024-2026 holdout is reported exactly as run; it is not used to tune parameters.
- External daily series are committed under `data/external/`.
hypothesis_md:
# Sector dispersion

**Slug:** `family-sector-dispersion`  
**Family:** sector-dispersion  
**Primary object:** Cross-sectional dispersion of 10 sector ETFs  
**Window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 development; full holdout 2024-01-02..2026-10-23.

## Claim

When sector dispersion is low, the market is moving on broad macro factors; buy TQQQ. When dispersion is high, hold BIL.

## Rules

- Signal uses the external daily series through the prior session; it is lagged one session.
- Target is written at the session close and filled at the next QQQ/TQQQ open.
- Long-only TQQQ/BIL, weights >=0, sum <=1, 2% band, 1 bp headline.
- 252-session percentile rank with a 0.45/0.55 deadband.
- No price-trend, realised-vol, calendar, opening-range, ML or risk-sizing gate.

## Falsifiers

- Full CAGR <=5% or fewer than 100 full fills (or 30 events).
- Signal Jaccard >0.70 against an existing winner.
- Raw daily-return correlation >0.70 against an existing winner.

## Caveat

The primary object is cross-sectional dispersion, not relative sector leadership. It is not a sector-rotation gate.
